title: Let's go on a trip!
situation: A friend texts you out of nowhere suggesting you two go on a trip together.
tip: When a friend floats a sudden idea, react with energy first (헐/완전) before getting into details. Matching their excitement keeps the plan alive.

turns.en: Hey, should we go on a trip or something?

turns.prompt: React with excitement and ask where

choices.en: Oh totally down! Where to?
choices.feedback: Reaction + follow-up question — exactly how a friend keeps the plan rolling.

choices.en: Would it be okay for us to go on a trip?
choices.feedback: Too formal (존댓말) and wishy-washy — sounds like you're asking a boss, not a friend.

choices.en: A trip? Out of nowhere?
choices.feedback: Sounds reluctant and puts the brakes on — it deflates their excitement instead of matching it.

turns.ko: 아직 안 정했어ㅋㅋ 그냥 어디든 떠나고 싶어
turns.en: Haven't decided yetㅋㅋ I just wanna get away somewhere.

turns.prompt: Agree and ask when they're thinking

choices.ko: 그 마음 너무 잘 알지ㅋㅋ 언제 갈 생각인데?
choices.en: I totally get that lol. When are you thinking of going?
choices.feedback: 그 마음 너무 잘 알지 agrees warmly, and the practical follow-up keeps the planning going.

choices.en: My schedule is still undecided.
choices.feedback: Stiff 존댓말 — way too businesslike for texting a close friend.

choices.en: What do you mean you wanna get away?
choices.feedback: Over-analyzing an obvious feeling — kills the vibe instead of going along with it.

turns.ko: 다음 달 초쯤? 너 주말에 시간 돼?
turns.en: Early next month maybe? You free on the weekend?

turns.prompt: Say you're free and push to lock it in

choices.ko: 오 나 그때 완전 괜찮아! 그럼 우리 진짜 가는 거다?
choices.en: Oh I'm totally good then! So we're really doing this?
choices.feedback: Confirms availability and seals the plan — energetic and decisive, just like a friend.

choices.ko: 시간 여부를 확인 후 다시 연락드리겠습니다.
choices.en: I'll check my availability and get back to you.
choices.feedback: Reads like a work email — far too formal and distant for a buddy.

choices.en: What day is the weekend again?
choices.feedback: Random and confusing — sidetracks the conversation instead of answering.

turns.ko: ㅋㅋㅋ 가는 거지! 내가 후보 몇 개 찾아볼게
turns.en: ㅋㅋㅋ we're going! I'll look up a few options.

turns.prompt: Show you're hyped and offer to help

choices.en: Deal! I'll look too haha can't wait.
choices.feedback: Enthusiastic agreement (콜) plus pitching in — perfect way to wrap a planning text.

choices.en: Understood. Please reply after reviewing.
choices.feedback: Sounds like a corporate memo — nobody texts a friend like this.

choices.en: I don't really know what 'options' means.
choices.feedback: Feigns confusion at a clear word — stalls the chat for no reason.

title: Busan or Jeju?
situation: You and a friend are texting to decide whether your trip should be to Busan or Jeju.
tip: When deciding between two options, share a real preference with a reason and bounce the question back (넌?). Casual chat is a back-and-forth, not a one-way vote.

turns.ko: 근데 우리 부산 갈까 제주 갈까?
turns.en: So should we go to Busan or Jeju?

turns.prompt: Give your lean and ask theirs

choices.ko: 음 난 바다 보고 싶어서 제주 끌리는데, 넌?
choices.en: Hmm I'm leaning Jeju 'cause I wanna see the ocean — you?
choices.feedback: States a preference with a reason and tosses it back — keeps the decision collaborative.

choices.en: May I ask which place you prefer?
choices.feedback: Overly polite 존댓말 — sounds like a survey, not two friends deciding.

choices.en: Should we go to Busan or Jeju?
choices.feedback: Just echoes their question — adds nothing and dodges the decision.

turns.ko: 오 제주 좋다! 근데 비행기값 비싸지 않나?
turns.en: Oh Jeju sounds good! But isn't the flight pricey?

choices.ko: 그것도 그렇네ㅋㅋ 그럼 부산도 괜찮아. 난 둘 다 좋아
choices.en: That's true too lol. Busan works for me then. I like both.
choices.feedback: 그것도 그렇네 accepts the budget concern, and 부산도 괜찮아 keeps the decision collaborative.

choices.en: I won't get involved regarding the flight cost.
choices.feedback: Cold and formal — sounds like dodging responsibility, not chatting with a friend.

choices.en: Is it your first time on a plane?
choices.feedback: Off-topic and a little odd — ignores the actual point about cost.

turns.ko: 흠 사실 난 부산 가서 회 먹고 싶긴 해
turns.en: Hmm honestly I kinda wanna go to Busan and eat sashimi.

turns.prompt: Get excited about the food angle

choices.ko: 헐 회 좋지!! 그럼 부산으로 가자, 먹킷리스트 짜자ㅋㅋ
choices.en: Whoa sashimi yes!! Let's do Busan then, let's make a food bucket listㅋㅋ
choices.feedback: Big reaction (헐) and runs with their idea toward a concrete next step — super natural.

choices.en: Sashimi is a healthy food.
choices.feedback: Random fact in textbook 존댓말 — kills the fun, friendly tone instantly.

choices.ko: 왜 갑자기 회 얘기를 하는 거야?
choices.en: Why are you suddenly talking about sashimi?
choices.feedback: Sounds annoyed at a normal suggestion — discourages your friend from sharing.

turns.ko: 콜콜 부산 가자!! 광안리에서 회에 소주 어때
turns.en: Deal deal, let's do Busan!! Sashimi and soju at Gwangalli, how about it?

turns.prompt: Lock it in and hype the plan

choices.ko: 캬 그거지ㅋㅋ 벌써 설렌다 빨리 가자
choices.en: Ahh that's the oneㅋㅋ I'm already excited, let's go soon.
choices.feedback: Playful interjection (캬) and shared excitement — a perfect upbeat closer.

choices.en: I will positively consider visiting Gwangalli.
choices.feedback: Bureaucratic 존댓말 — completely wrong register for hyping a trip with a friend.

choices.en: Is there nothing besides soju?
choices.feedback: Nitpicks a casual suggestion — dampens the excitement they just shared.

title: Locking down the stay & plans
situation: Now that the destination is set, you and a friend text to sort out the accommodation and rough itinerary.
tip: When working out logistics, give a clear opinion but offer to share the load (내가 ~할게). Friends split tasks and check in with each other rather than just demanding.

turns.ko: 숙소는 어디로 잡지? 호텔 아니면 에어비앤비?
turns.en: Where should we book to stay? Hotel or Airbnb?

turns.prompt: Give a clear pick with a reason

choices.ko: 난 에어비앤비! 우리끼리 편하게 놀 수 있잖아
choices.en: I say Airbnb! We can just chill comfortably on our own.
choices.feedback: Clear preference with a quick reason — decisive and friendly, moves planning along.

choices.en: I shall defer to your decision on the accommodation.
choices.feedback: Absurdly formal 존댓말 — sounds like a contract, not two friends planning a trip.

choices.en: Which is better, a hotel or an Airbnb?
choices.feedback: Bounces the same question back without committing — stalls the decision.

turns.ko: 오 좋아 에어비앤비 콜! 그럼 내가 찾아볼까?
turns.en: Oh nice, Airbnb it is! Should I look one up then?

choices.ko: 오키 그럼 숙소는 네가, 맛집은 내가 찾을게!
choices.en: Okay then you take the stay, I'll find the restaurants!
choices.feedback: Divides the tasks (네가 / 내가) — exactly how friends share the load casually.

choices.en: I shall entrust that task to you.
choices.feedback: Stiff, work-style 존댓말 — way too formal for divvying up trip chores.

choices.en: Why are YOU looking for the place?
choices.feedback: Sounds suspicious of a kind offer — discourages your friend from helping.

turns.en: Good good lol, but are we doing one night and two days or two nights and three days?

turns.prompt: Suggest longer and check with them

choices.ko: 이왕 가는 거 2박 3일 어때? 1박 2일은 너무 짧잖아
choices.en: Since we're going anyway, how about two nights and three days? One night and two days is too short.
choices.feedback: Offers a specific longer plan, then gives a clear reason and checks with 어때.

choices.en: The trip duration will be announced at a later date.
choices.feedback: Reads like an official notice — totally out of place between friends.

choices.en: How many days is one night?
choices.feedback: Confuses a basic term — derails the chat and sounds clueless.

turns.en: Okay two nights, love it! Let's party hard from day oneㅋㅋ

turns.prompt: Match the energy and wrap up

choices.ko: ㅋㅋㅋ 좋아, 맛집 리스트 짜서 공유할게! 완전 기대된다
choices.en: Lol, nice. I'll make a restaurant list and share it! I'm so excited.
choices.feedback: This keeps the earlier task split, confirms the next step, and ends with matching excitement.

choices.ko: 일정표 작성 완료 시 송부해 드리겠습니다.
choices.en: I will dispatch the itinerary upon completion.
choices.feedback: Sounds like a memo to a client — wrong register for texting a friend.

choices.en: What does partying hard even mean?
choices.feedback: Questions an obvious phrase — flattens the hyped mood instead of matching it.
